design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — warranty_claims_service task 0 (Renata Whitfield, kitchen flooring cash settlement)

0. DRAW AND SCOPE SNAPSHOT (Step 0)
- draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"task": 0, "key": "env_0033_national_homebuilder/warranty_claims_service/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 5]}. --tasks 2 also printed task 1: prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [6, 6, 6].
- Occupied before this task: nothing (first task). Claimed here: warranty_ext_missed_appointment_charge (4 factors, agent tool assess_missed_appointment_charge_27486c7f) and warranty_ext_finish_item_settlement (5 factors, user tool accept_finish_item_cash_settlement_135d939d).
- Headroom left for task 1 (3 problems x 6 factors, needs its own owner=user problem): the reinspection fee (warranty_tolerances_and_exclusions sentence 'An item already denied within_tolerance that is re-reported and again measured within tolerance carries reinspection_fee_usd'), the emergency dispatch fee (warranty_appointment_charges sentence 'An emergency dispatch that finds a condition caused by the homeowner or not covered carries emergency_dispatch_fee_usd') and the cash settlement of a covered systems item (warranty_payouts_and_payments cash in lieu, owner=user, split from the finish-item settlement by item basis). None of them is touched here; the missed-appointment charge and the finish-item settlement are not reused there.
- Why the user problem is a cash settlement: the blueprint makes 'accepting a cash settlement instead of a repair' the homeowner's own written decision and lists every other warranty write (claims, decisions, appointments, charges, waivers, payouts) as agent work; payments of charges carry no computable figure of their own. So both trees put a homeowner cash-in-lieu acceptance on the customer's side; this task takes the finish (workmanship) item, task 1 the systems item.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST
The customer asks for one thing: cash instead of another repair on her kitchen floor (WSR-51847-02). The settlement policy hides a prerequisite the customer never mentions: 'The finish settlement is fixed only after every missed appointment on the coverage that the missed-appointment rules make chargeable carries its missed-appointment charge.' The agent must (a) read that sentence, (b) find in the ledger that the 2026-09-29 miss on the cabinet item WSR-51592-01 (an original-approval item with no accepted callback) carries no charge, (c) work out from the missed-appointment rules that it IS chargeable (4 recorded misses, 1 waived -> counted 3, minus 1 free = billable 2), (d) compute that charge (87.89) with four factors, book it, and only then (e) compute the settlement (925.04) with five factors, one of which (service delay) reads the charge just booked. Difficulty = discovering the prerequisite + reconciling 54 warranty rows and 11 design rows + two multi-factor calculations; no near-synonym tools exist (one charge tool, one settlement tool).
Depth: surface goal -> finish settlement rule -> its prerequisite sentence -> missed-appointment rule (counting convention, free allowance) -> charge write -> settlement write. Breadth: two cross-difficulty reads (purchase community, design package and option ledger), four history windows (life misses, 12-month and 6-month charge windows, 12-month callbacks), the 24-month aging window, booking lead time, item category, approval age vs repair target days.

2. BASE-INVARIANT CARD
- Charge write (subject warranty_charge_assessed): governing base policies warranty_appointment_charges, warranty_tolerances_and_exclusions, warranty_structural_claims, warranty_transfer. None has an eligibility gate applying to warranty_charge_assessed (the only gate of warranty_appointment_charges, one_waiver_per_charge, applies to waivers), so all four enter base_preconditions as policy_scope with their scope reasoning. Inherited clauses: the charge is linked to the claim item; only misses beyond the free allowance carry a charge. Superseded (declared in overwrite): 'Each missed appointment beyond free_missed_appointments over the life of the home's coverage (warranty_msr_missed_appointments, counted including the one being recorded) carries missed_appointment_fee_usd, linked to the claim item.' replaced by the multiplier sentence; the base fee (75.00) and free allowance (1) stay base params. Extra lineage warranty_agg_one_owner_per_home (counting across owners) cited only as input lineage.
- Settlement write (subject warranty_payout_approved): governing base policies warranty_payouts_and_payments ('In place of repairing a covered non-structural item, Calloway may offer a cash settlement of no more than cash_in_lieu_max_usd per claim item; it becomes a payout only when the homeowner accepts it in writing') and warranty_structural_claims (relocation payouts; not this payout). No gate applies -> policy_scope x2. overwrite [] because base fixes only the ceiling (1,000.00 for Preferred), and the extended figure 925.04 stays under it; the 'written acceptance' is carried by the owner=user tool.
- No time gate is touched by either write (the coverage-period gates apply to warranty_claim_approved only), so temporal_feasibility is []. Coverage facts at frozen_time 2026-10-05: workmanship end 2027-03-13 (the flooring item was approved inside it: original 2026-04-29, callback 2026-07-15 within 60 callback days of the 2026-05-12 repair: 55 days).

3. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
- Charge object: the 2026-09-29 missed repair appointment on claim item WSR-51592-01, the warped pantry cabinet door (scheduled row booked 2026-09-25; one original approval 2026-06-10, no callback). Rows entering the counting: the 4 warranty_appointment_missed rows (2025-06-12 WSR-50312-01 free; 2025-11-18 WSR-50731-01 charged WCH-50417 37.50 and waived calloway_rescheduled 2025-11-20; 2026-03-24 WSR-51135-01 charged WCH-51268 75.00, paid card WRC-53071 2026-04-02; 2026-09-29 WSR-51592-01 uncharged). Rows excluded: scheduled rows of other dates (notice reads only the booking whose appointment_date equals the missed date). Correlation key written back: claim_item_ref WSR-51592-01.
- Settlement object: claim item WSR-51847-02 under the latest workmanship approval (callback approval 2026-07-15, callback_seq 1). Other approvals on the coverage are older (WSR-51847-01 2026-04-29 repaired; WSR-51135-01, WSR-50731-01, WSR-50312-01, WSR-50288-01 all repaired). Correlation key written back: claim_item_ref WSR-51847-02.

4. PROBLEM-TREE CARD
- Root warranty_ext_finish_item_settlement (on_request, owner=user tool accept_finish_item_cash_settlement_135d939d) <- warranty_ext_missed_appointment_charge (state_due, agent tool assess_missed_appointment_charge_27486c7f).
- Edge: kind value_input, gate delay_mult (service-delay multiplier), form state. policy_source (verbatim in the root's own rule): 'The finish settlement is fixed only after every missed appointment on the coverage that the missed-appointment rules make chargeable carries its missed-appointment charge.' Four-point test: (1) ordering connective 'only after', affirmative direction, chosen because a settlement figure is 'fixed only after' what it rests on is complete; (2) the waited-on side is a record-visible state (chargeable misses carrying a missed-appointment charge), no action, performer or tool named; (3) no tool name, policy id or code token; (4) scope 'every ... chargeable' = exactly the condition (misses the counting convention leaves billable). Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only the missed-appointment charge policy books missed_appointment_fee charges (the reinspection and dispatch charges of task 1 book other charge types). Derivation: sentence + ledger (4 misses, 1 waived, charges only on WSR-50731-01 and WSR-51135-01) + the missed-appointment rule (counting convention, billable number, 'linked to that appointment's claim item') -> the one resolving action is booking a missed-appointment charge for WSR-51592-01.
- Why false at frozen_time: initial_state warranty_events m4 (appointment_date 2026-09-29, claim_item_ref WSR-51592-01) has no charge; the two missed_appointment_fee rows carry WSR-50731-01 and WSR-51135-01. Flips true by the step-8 write.
- Deletion sensitivity (verify.py skip run): without step 8 the settlement recomputes 983.00 (delay 1.25) instead of 925.04 (delay 1.10), and the charge row (87.89) and charges_due 87.89 are missing.
- Topological order: charge (step 8) -> settlement (step 10); single edge, no parallel branch.
- user_scenario never names a charge, fee, balance or prerequisite; tools validate no prerequisite (both just create the row and update the running balance).

5. FACTOR CARD (on the handling-time world)
Missed-appointment charge (draw 4): baseline = 'every missed appointment counted; billable number = count - free; fee 75.00 when billable >= 1' -> 75.00.
 F1 miss_count_convention (method; tiers: waived charge exists -> life less waived / no waiver and coverage >= 24 months -> last 24 months only / otherwise life): tier 1, count 3; baseline count 4 -> 105.47. Evidence: 4 missed rows, 1 waiver row. Near-miss: the waived 2025-11-18 miss (a reader who counts it gets billable 3 and 1.50).
 F2 notice_multiplier (parameter; <2 days 0.50 / 2-6 days 0.75 / >=7 days 1.00): booked 2026-09-25 for 2026-09-29 = 4 days -> 0.75; baseline 117.19.
 F3 trade_trip_multiplier (parameter; plumbing/electrical/hvac 1.50 / flooring, tile, cabinets_countertops 1.25 / other 1.00): cabinets_countertops -> 1.25; baseline 70.31.
 F4 repeat_miss_multiplier (parameter, multi-source: billable number AND unwaived charges of the last 12 months; >=3 -> 1.50, ==2 -> 1.25, else 1.00): billable 2, unwaived 1 -> 1.25; baseline 70.31.
 All-baseline fall-back 75.00 != 87.89.
Finish-item settlement (draw 5): baseline 'cash-in-lieu maximum x standard share 0.45' -> 450.00.
 G1 settlement_share (parameter; flooring/tile/cabinets_countertops 0.60 / paint/drywall/trim 0.30 / other 0.45): flooring -> 0.60; baseline 818.78.
 G2 labor_market_multiplier (parameter, cross-difficulty purchase.community; Sierra Vista Ranch 1.25 / Larkspur Meadows or Willow Bend Reserve 1.12 / other 1.00): Larkspur Meadows -> 1.12; baseline 879.50.
 G3 finish_level_multiplier (parameter, multi-source + cross-difficulty design: package AND net finish upgrades): Studio Designer, 11,870 -> 1.15; baseline 869.60. Near-miss: removed countertop line 2,600 (keeping it gives 14,470 -> 1.30) and the electrical line 1,850 (not a finish category).
 G4 service_delay_multiplier (parameter, multi-source: days since latest workmanship approval vs repair target AND unwaived missed-appointment charges of 6 months): 82 > 21 and 1 charge (the step-8 charge) -> 1.10; baseline 886.40. Near-miss: WCH-51268 of 2026-03-24 is exactly 6 whole months old and outside the window.
 G5 callback_settlement_method (method; >=2 callbacks in 12 months -> maximum / 1 -> midpoint / 0 -> scheduled): 1 callback (2026-07-06) -> midpoint; baseline 850.08. Near-miss: the 2025-07-08 callback (14 months old).
 All-baseline fall-back 450.00 != 925.04.
No outcome stamp exists in the schema for any factor; every tier is derived from ledger rows, dates or the other products' records.

6. WORLD (initial_state) AND WHY EACH ROW CLASS EXISTS
- customers (1): identity (phone 7205550186, ssn 8613, zip 80108, email) inside this difficulty's band.
- purchase_agreements (1, closed Crestview Collection, Larkspur Meadows, LM-0527): parent of the coverage and design file; community feeds G2 (remove it and the market multiplier falls to 1.00).
- design_selections (1, Studio Designer, delivered) + design_events (11): package and option ledger feed G3; deposit/credit rows make the file's balances consistent (option_total 13,720 = 6,840+3,150+2,600+1,850+1,880-2,600; deposits 3,892.50 paid and applied at closing; allowance 6,000 granted and applied). Delivered file: no design obligation opens.
- warranty_coverages (1): Preferred program; charges_due 0.00 and payouts_owed 0.00 reconcile with the ledger.
- warranty_events (54): five claim histories, walkthroughs (sixty-day 2025-05-09, HVAC check 2025-10-14, eleven-month 2026-02-10; the twenty-three-month window opens 2027-01-13, after frozen_time), four misses, two charges, one waiver, one payment, two callbacks. Historical charges obey the extended rule on their own dates: 2025-11-18 (count 2, billable 1, notice 1 day -> 0.50, trim -> 37.50); 2026-03-24 (count 3-1=2, billable 1, notice 20 days, paint -> 75.00), so the ledger teaches no contrary algorithm.
- Automatic clauses checked: the access window (14 days) after the 2026-09-29 miss runs to 2026-10-13, after frozen_time, so no no_access closure is owed; no payout is approved-but-unissued; no charge is open; coverage active; callbacks inside windows. The only debt lit by the seed is the 2026-09-29 missed-appointment charge, carried by this task.

7. PERSONA DESIGN
Brisk travelling operations manager; volunteers only the surface goal (cash instead of another repair on the kitchen floor), the story of the May repair and July recurrence, and that she will sign herself. Given only when asked: phone, SSN last four, ZIP/email fallback, item number WSR-51847-02, and the admission that she missed the 2026-09-29 cabinet-door appointment (WSR-51592-01). Passive reactions: agrees generically if told something else must be recorded first; declines a rebooking; signs the acceptance with exactly the values the agent gives; ends after the receipt. She knows no figure, never corrects, raises no further ask (no payment, no copy by email). Authority: no internal status is volunteered as fact beyond what the ledger shows (repair in May, recurrence, approval).

8. STANDARD SOLUTION
find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, ssn) -> find_warranty_coverages -> find_warranty_ledger -> find_purchase_agreements -> find_design_files -> find_design_ledger -> unlock + call assess_missed_appointment_charge_27486c7f(coverage, WSR-51592-01, 87.89) -> unlock_user + (customer) call accept_finish_item_cash_settlement_135d939d(coverage, WSR-51847-02, 925.04).

9. VERIFICATION (Step 5) — _authoring/verify.py (reuses check_compute's build_env/eval_compute; replays gold writes in order, fills expected, runs factor and edge sensitivity). Output:
 missed-appointment charge step 8: result 87.89; factor baselines 105.47 / 117.19 / 70.31 / 70.31; all-baseline 75.00.
 finish settlement step 10: result 925.04; factor baselines 818.78 / 879.50 / 869.60 / 886.40 / 850.08; all-baseline 450.00.
 skip edge: with 925.04, without 983.00.
Gates run (--task 0): EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK (11 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous, closure 69 = init 69); SOLVABILITY OK (6 base gates, 55 seed rows); COMPUTE OK (9 factors, 2 cross, 20 history rows, 29 branches); GROUNDING OK; SCOPE OK; CACHE-DIFF INFO (no cache trap used). check_traceability awaits the published KB.
Revision log: (1) symptom: check_extended flagged module helper '_printed_number' as an unnamed task tool -> root cause: helper defined at module level -> change: inlined the printed-number expression in each tool -> re-run EXTENDED OK. (2) docstrings contained ordering words ('before', 'after', 'afterwards') -> reworded. (3) persona originally named 'a charge for an appointment you missed' in a reaction -> generalised to 'something else has to be recorded', so no prerequisite is named.

10. SOLVABILITY CONTRACT vs GT
Step 8: state_due, intent from the initial_state missed row; stage preexisting_before_conversation (the miss is a recorded past event); policy_scope x4. Step 10: on_request, discriminator 'take the cash instead of another repair on the kitchen floor' verbatim in user_scenario; stage performed_by_this_tool (the written acceptance happens in the call); policy_scope x2. Each argument traced (argument_uniqueness_tracing).

11. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT
Masking compute/expected/GT and reading only the rule prose, tool schemas, finder returns and persona lines: the settlement rule's prerequisite sentence sends the reader to the missed-appointment rule; the ledger shows the 2026-09-29 miss uncharged; the counting convention (waived charge present -> 4-1=3), free allowance 1 -> billable 2 -> charge 75 x 0.75 x 1.25 x 1.25 = 87.89; then the settlement on WSR-51847-02: 1,000 x 0.60 x 1.12 x 1.15 x 1.10 = 850.08, one callback -> 925.04. Same object, order and figures as gold; no second reading found (the only judgement calls — which miss, which item, which design lines — are each pinned by a rule sentence).

12. MANUAL VALUES GATES (task 0)
Length/breadth: two hops, each with its own multi-factor calculation; owner=user write is genuine (written acceptance) and completes on the spot. Need/simulator boundary: object (kitchen floor item), timing (today), authorisation (she signs; agent books whatever must be recorded) all explicit. Chronology: volunteered facts (May repair, July recurrence, approval, back-order talk) are backed by repair 2026-05-12, callback 2026-07-06, approval 2026-07-15 and the long gap to the 2026-09-25 booking. No real-world wait: both writes are synchronous. Prerequisite sentence: state form, one direction chosen by the business voice ('fixed only after'); the charter's other sentences in task 1 use the negated direction too. Rule/compute equivalence swept both ways (compute_basis quotes every reading or choosing binding; every quantity sentence of each rule is claimed). Factors honest: each baseline is what the computation document states; method factors change how a count or the settlement is taken, not a rate.

ROUND 2 REWORK (policy-task audit audits/policy_task/warranty_claims_service/: _difficulty.md, 0.md and 1.md read in full; every RED item and observation closed here or in task 1's round-2 section)
- F2 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, this task: base warranty_callbacks 'An accepted callback ... carries no deductible or fee' conflicted with charging a miss on an accepted callback's repair appointment). Closed in both the charter and the world, and not by overriding base. Charter: warranty_callbacks added to the missed-appointment policy's base_policy_refs; its rule now carries 'A missed appointment whose claim item has an accepted callback still awaiting its repair (more callback approvals than callback repairs recorded on that item) carries no charge, because an accepted callback carries no fee; such a miss is still counted among the coverage's missed appointments.' Compute: new cb_approvals, cb_repairs and callback_open, and result 0.0 when callback_open. World: the 2026-09-25 booking and the 2026-09-29 miss (rows 6f36e117, 1b32e724) now belong to a separate original-approval item, WSR-51592-01 (cabinets_countertops, warped pantry cabinet door). It has new rows: filed 2026-06-01, inspected 2026-06-09 defect_confirmed, approved 2026-06-10 callback_seq 0, and no callback, so the exception does not reach the charged miss and the callback reading no longer yields a second answer. The flooring item WSR-51847-02 keeps its accepted callback (2026-07-06, approved 2026-07-15) with no appointment, and remains the settlement's item as the latest workmanship approval. Same counts, notice (4 days) and trade tier (cabinets_countertops, specialty finish installer 1.25), so the charge stays 87.89 and the settlement 925.04. Propagated to: eval step 3 objective/necessity, step 8 argument claim_item_ref and objective, step 8 tracing, solvability gold_actions[0] (discriminator value, semantics, stage fact), seed_consistency (2 rewritten + 3 new rows), prerequisite_closure (why_false, evidence, flips, skipped_effect), factor_trace (plus a callback-exception plumbing line), and the persona (asked-only admission now about the cabinet-door appointment, explicitly not part of her request).
- F1 (latent: undeclared cross-owner count). Declared: overwrite now names warranty_agg_one_owner_per_home 'Every owner of the home shares the same coverage start date and coverage end dates, and history that counts over the life of the coverage (missed appointments, one-time repairs) counts across owners of the same home.', replaced_by the new rule sentence 'For the missed-appointment charge only the missed appointments recorded on the homeowner's own coverage are counted, never those recorded on a previous owner's coverage of the same home, while every owner of the home still shares the coverage start and end dates and one-time repairs still count across owners.' This keeps the shared dates and one-time repairs inherited, and gives life_misses its compute_basis. Both tasks are original buyers, so no figure moves.
- F3 (latent: design XSUM not scoped to the home's file). Compute adds design_file = CFIELD('design','selection_id', purchase_id=F('purchase_id')), and all six finish XSUMs filter selection_id=design_file, matching 'the Design Studio Selections file of the home's purchase agreement'. Task 0 has one file, so the finish upgrades stay 11,870.
- O1 (waiver counts not filtered by charge type): kept. Base warranty_appointment_charges allows a waiver only for a missed appointment that followed Calloway's short-notice reschedule (waiver_reason has the single value calloway_rescheduled), so every waiver row is a missed-appointment waiver and the two readings coincide.
- O4 (finish edge effect worded too broadly): effect reworded to 'reads one more unwaived charge in its six-month window; where the repair target days have passed and no other unwaived missed-appointment charge of that window stood, it moves from the no-unwaived-charge tier to the at-least-one-unwaived-charge tier'.
- O5 (LATEST same-date ties): no LATEST of either task resolves on a tie. The two 2026-04-29 workmanship approvals are not the latest; the new cabinet approval (2026-06-10) is dated alone. Recorded only.
- O2 and O3 and the task 1 items (F4, F5, F6, F7) are closed in task 1's round-2 section. The O2 docstring change ('already rounded to the nearest cent') applies to both tools here as well.
- Re-run after rework: verify.py 0 --fill gives the missed-appointment charge 87.89 (factor baselines 105.47/117.19/70.31/70.31; all 75.00) and the settlement 925.04 (818.78/879.50/869.60/886.40/850.08; all 450.00); skip edge 983.00. Full gate block in the final run (no --task): EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, CACHE-DIFF INFO, SCOPE OK; TRACEABILITY awaits the rendered KB.

ROUND 3 REWORK (audit revision_2 sections of _difficulty.md, 0.md and 1.md read in full; both tasks marked PASS there; the items closed in revision_2 (F1-F7, O2, O4) were left untouched)
- N1 (charter SOURCE-POLICY RED, latent: the finish edge `condition` was broader than its prerequisite sentence after the callback exemption). Root cause: the condition still required a charge row for every miss with billable number >= 1. Change: warranty_ext_finish_item_settlement.prerequisite[0].condition now covers only misses 'that the missed-appointment rules make chargeable (billable number one or more, and its appointment date not falling while its claim item had an accepted callback awaiting repair)', and says a miss the rules leave uncharged needs no row. It is copied verbatim into prerequisite_closure.edges[0].condition here. The sentence is unchanged; condition and sentence now have the same scope.
- O6 (latent: the callback exemption was judged on the assessment day, not at the time of the miss). Change: the rule sentence now reads 'A missed appointment that fell while its claim item had an accepted callback awaiting repair (the item's latest callback is dated on or before the missed appointment date, and the item's latest repair is either dated on or before that callback or dated on or after the missed appointment date) carries no charge, because an accepted callback carries no fee; such a miss is still counted among the coverage's missed appointments.' The compute replaces cb_approvals/cb_repairs with last_callback = LATEST callback date on the item and last_repair = LATEST repair date on the item, and callback_open applies the date test, so a miss on a callback repair appointment stays exempt even after that repair is completed. compute_basis is re-quoted verbatim. On this world the charged item WSR-51592-01 has no callback, so callback_open is false and the charge and settlement figures are unchanged (COMPUTE OK recomputes every expected value and factor_sensitivity figure).
- O7, O8 and N2 concern task 1's policies (see that task's round-3 section). O1, O3 and O5 stay recorded as in revision_2.
- Gates re-run after round 3: per task (--task 0/1): EXTENDED OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK. Full block (no --task): EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, CACHE-DIFF INFO, SCOPE OK; TRACEABILITY NOT OK only for the five hidden tool names, which need the rendered KB.
user_scenario: You are Renata Whitfield, a regional operations manager who travels for work most weeks and owns a Calloway home in Larkspur Meadows, Castle Rock, Colorado, that you bought new and closed on in March 2025. You are calling on your lunch break, organised and a little clipped, the way you talk to a vendor who has missed a deadline, but never rude. Your reason for calling: the vinyl plank flooring by your kitchen island is lifting and separating again. Calloway's flooring crew fixed it in May, it came back in July, Calloway approved it as a warranty item again, and since then you have mostly heard that the planks were back-ordered. You are done waiting: you want to take the cash instead of another repair on the kitchen floor and have your own flooring installer deal with it. You are asking for the cash settlement on that one kitchen flooring item only, today, and you will sign the acceptance yourself; you are not asking Calloway to schedule anything else, and you do not want any other item on the house touched or changed. You open by giving your name and saying, in your own words, that you want to take the cash for the kitchen floor instead of another repair. When the agent asks how to find your account, give your mobile number, 7205550186. If the agent asks you to confirm your identity, give the last four digits of your Social Security number, 8613; if they need one more item, your ZIP code is 80108 and your email is renata.whitfield@gmail.com. You do not remember your date of birth being on file and you would rather not give it; if pressed, say you would prefer to use the ZIP code. If the agent asks which item it is, read it off the service request in your email: the kitchen floor is item WSR-51847-02 (the pantry door latch, WSR-51847-01, was on the same request and was fixed fine in May). Only if the agent asks about the cabinet repair appointment on September 29, admit that you were not home for it because a work trip ran late, and that it was your fault; that appointment was for a warped pantry cabinet door, item WSR-51592-01, which is still waiting for a new door and is not part of what you are calling about. You do not know how Calloway works out a settlement or any of its fees, you have no figure in mind, and you never suggest a number. If the agent explains that something else has to be recorded on your account before the settlement figure can be fixed, you sigh, say that if it is what the rules require then fine, and tell them to go ahead; you do not ask to pay anything on this call and you do not argue it. If the agent offers to book another repair instead, decline politely and repeat that you would rather have the cash. When the agent tells you the settlement amount and hands you the acceptance to sign, sign it yourself using exactly the coverage reference number, the item number and the amount the agent gives you, without changing any of them. Once the acceptance shows as recorded, thank the agent briefly and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's buyer/homeowner profile from the mobile number she gives.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write is keyed by the customer reference number this lookup returns; nothing can be discussed before the profile is found.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Confirm the caller is Renata Whitfield with two matching items (mobile number and last four of the SSN).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Account details may not be discussed and no charge or settlement may be recorded until identity passes the 2-item threshold.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her HomeCare 2-3-10 Preferred coverage: coverage reference number, coverage start date 2025-03-14 and the purchase agreement of the home.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The program sets the missed-appointment fee, the free missed appointments, the repair target days and the cash-in-lieu maximum; the coverage start date feeds the missed-appointment counting convention; the coverage id is the target of both writes.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull the whole warranty history: the four missed appointments, the waived and the paid missed-appointment charges, the cabinet item WSR-51592-01 with its booking of 2026-09-25 and its missed repair appointment of 2026-09-29, the flooring item WSR-51847-02 with its callback and its latest workmanship approval of 2026-07-15, and the callbacks of the last 12 months.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: This read discovers the unmet prerequisite (the 2026-09-29 miss on WSR-51592-01, an original-approval item with no open accepted callback, is chargeable under the missed-appointment rules but carries no charge, while the finish-settlement rule says the settlement 'is fixed only after every missed appointment on the coverage that the missed-appointment rules make chargeable carries its missed-appointment charge') and supplies every evidence row of the counting convention, notice, trade trip and repeat-miss factors and of the settlement share, service-delay and callback factors.

Factors: program fee P(missed_appointment_fee_usd) = 75.00 (HomeCare 2-3-10 Preferred); counting convention: a waived charge exists (WCH-50417) so count = 4 recorded misses - 1 waived = 3, billable number = 3 - 1 free = 2; notice multiplier 0.75 (booked 2026-09-25 for 2026-09-29, 4 days); trade trip multiplier 1.25 (cabinets and countertops item); repeat-miss multiplier 1.25 (billable number 2 and 1 unwaived missed-appointment charge in the 12 months: 2 assessed - 1 waived). 75.00 x 0.75 x 1.25 x 1.25 = 87.890625, rounded once at the end -> 87.89. edges.condition: Every warranty_appointment_missed row on the coverage that the missed-appointment rules make chargeable (billable number one or more, and its appointment date not falling while its claim item had an accepted callback awaiting repair) is matched by a warranty_charge_assessed row of charge_type missed_appointment_fee on the same claim item; a miss the rules leave uncharged needs no such row.
edges.policy_source: The finish settlement is fixed only after every missed appointment on the coverage that the missed-appointment rules make chargeable carries its missed-appointment charge.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The coverage records four missed appointments (2025-06-12, 2025-11-18, 2026-03-24, 2026-09-29) and one waived missed-appointment charge, so under the missed-appointment rules the 2026-09-29 miss on WSR-51592-01 (an item with one original approval and no callback, so the callback-fee exception does not reach it) counts as 3 with a billable number of 2 (HomeCare 2-3-10 Preferred allows 1 free miss) and is chargeable; the only missed-appointment charges on the coverage are WCH-50417 (claim item WSR-50731-01, the 2025-11-18 miss) and WCH-51268 (WSR-51135-01, the 2026-03-24 miss). No charge is linked to WSR-51592-01, so the state the finish settlement waits on does not hold at frozen_time.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The missed-appointment charge write books a warranty_charge_assessed row (charge_type missed_appointment_fee, claim_item_ref WSR-51592-01, amount 87.89, event_date 2026-10-05); every chargeable miss then carries its charge, and the finish settlement's unwaived missed-appointment charges of the last 6 months go from 0 to 1, moving the service-delay multiplier from 1.25 to 1.10 (verified: settlement 983.00 without the charge, 925.04 with it).

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single edge: the finish settlement depends on the missed-appointment charge and nothing else, so the only topological order is charge first, settlement second. The reverse order is not a second solution: written first, the settlement reads no unwaived missed-appointment charge in the last 6 months and computes 983.00 instead of 925.04 (verified by the skip run), so the terminal payout row differs.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the missed-appointment charge (step 8) and replaying everything else: the missed_appointment_fee row for WSR-51592-01 (87.89) is absent and coverage charges_due stays 0.00 instead of 87.89; the finish settlement at step 10 recomputes 983.00 (service-delay multiplier 1.25, no unwaived charge in 6 months) instead of 925.04 (1.10), so the cash_in_lieu payout amount and payouts_owed change.
